steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Coat the bottom and sides of a 1 ½-quart casserole dish with 1 tablespoon olive oil.

Heat remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir garlic until fragrant and golden brown. Add eggplant and parsley; cook and stir until eggplant is tender and soft, about 10 minutes. Season with salt to taste.

Spread eggplant mixture evenly across the bottom of the prepared casserole dish; sprinkle with a few tablespoons of Parmesan cheese. Spread zucchini in an even layer over top. Lightly salt and sprinkle with a little more cheese. Continue layering in this fashion, with tomatoes, mushrooms, onion, and bell pepper, covering each layer with a sprinkling of salt and cheese.
Bake in preheated oven until vegetables are tender, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Ratatouille
raw_recipe.description: This ratatouille recipe with ripe summer tomatoes, zucchini, eggplant, and bell pepper is a delicious version of the classic French vegetable stew.

review.reviewBody:
This is a flavorful, hearty recipe, but very low calorie. I served it as a main dish with couscous to soak up the liquid. 

Like many other reviewers, I made a few adjustments based on the availability ingredients, and prices at the supermarket, but nothing major:
*I cooked everything in a crock pot on low for 8 hours (the house smelled wonderful!)
*I added only a little freshly grated romano cheese just before serving, instead of parmesan as the recipe calls for
*I added yellow squash in addition to the zucchini

I had enough ratatouille for dinner for my husband and myself, lunch the next day, dinner several days later, and frozen portions for an easy dinner this winter. 

Great recipe!

After watching the Disney Movie "Ratatouille". My kids wanted to make the dish. I cut up all the veggies with a mandoline and let them layer everything into a baking dish. It was a wonderful accompaniment to parmesean chicken. Thanks for a wonderful recipe. Who would have thought a Disney movie would make my kids eager to eat their veggies.

Excellent vegetarian dish! Instead of cooking it in the oven, I just sauteed the whole thing. I first cooked garlic and onion in olive oil, added the rest of the ingredients, put the cover on and cooked until the vegetables were tender (about 30+ minutes). Some changes I have made: One large tomato and one can of diced tomato instead of 2 tomatoes, added some basil, pinch of red pepper flakes and a drizzle of olive oil at the end, and sprinkled freshly grated romano cheese right before serving instead of mixing parmesan into the vegetables.

Will make it again!

Made this twice, and I feel a few little tips makes this go from great to fabulous. First, use a lot of eggplant (use a large eggplant, not a small or medium) as this is the "top" flavor. Press the garlic rather than mince for a bold garlic flavor in the eggplant. Remove the eggplant from the saute pan then lightly brown the onions in the same pan. If it's sticky, add a little water, but be sure to keep the browned bits from the eggplant/garlic mixture. This flavors the onions like you can't believe. Use both yellow and green zucchini squash if you can. Use FRESHLY grated Parmesan cheese. Use red, orange, or yellow bell pepper instead of the green to add a nice sweetness. Other than than, follow the recipe as written. It's really yummy!

Wow! I was looking forward to trying the leftovers after reading these reviews, but there weren't any! My kids (thanks to THE movie) wolfed it all down. The cat even licked out the bowl. I made this once before (pre-kids) and don't remember it being this good. Thanks for the wonderful recipe. It went perfectly with a nice loaf of crusty sourdough bread.

A couple of notes: be generous with the garlic. I used 3 large cloves with one medium-sized eggplant. I also used fresh parsley from my garden (2 tbsp). I forgot to get the mushrooms, but added one yellow squash to the layers. Remember to slice all the vegies THINLY (about 1/8") making the ratatouille cook through in 45 minutes in an 8 x 10" pan. (It shrinks quite a bit from cooking.) I also sliced the tomatoes thinly and placed them on top, using Asiago cheese throughout. It was fantasticly moist with a delicious broth. I'll be making this again (certainly at my kids' request!). Who would have ever guessed that they would ever ask for something WITHOUT meat made WITH eggplant, green peppers, and squash? Hallelujah!

A delicious recipe! I would suggest cutting the onion rings into smaller pieces, same with the peppers. In my opinion the salting between layers is completely unnecessary, I stopped salting after the first layer. Used a mandolin slicer to get uniform slide for the veggies except mushrooms and peppers. I used fresh grated Parmesan cheese and it added plenty of salt favoring. I only cooked for 30 minutes, my zucchini was still tender crisp, loved everything about the side. Tasty and satisfying. The only thing I added was some Jimmy Dean sage sausage which I browned and crumbled. Also used a gourmet mushroom pack as no crimini's at my grocery store. Would definitely make again. Any veggies can be used to clear out the refrain.

I haven't tried this exact recipe, BUT I've made a stripped down version of it stove top for decades. In a large pot/dutch oven on medium high put in a little oil, and add 1 diced potato, 1 chopped onion, 1 chopped green pepper, 1 peeled and diced eggplant, 1 chopped zucchini or calabacitas squash, 4 chopped tomatoes, salt and pepper as desired. Cover and simmer for 1-1 1/2 hours. Stir occasionally, scraping the bottom. Uncover towards the end if you want less liquid (which I prefer), or you can leave it slushy to go over rice, for example. It can also be cooked in a slow cooker. It makes A LOT. I usually eat as a generous serving over a slice or two of whole wheat bread (Orowheat 12 Grain). I don't add Parmesan, but i love it with feta on the side. It's a meal in itself. You could also have it over spaghetti, or mixed into meatloaf, or whatever you want. However, this sounds like a good variation. I'll have to try it.

Delicious flavors. The only thing was that the eggplant made the dish very liquidy . I read somewhere if you salt the eggplant and leave it sit for 30 mins, all the moisture will be drawn out and you can drain it first. I will try that next time.
Delicious vegetarian dish! I took some tips from other reviews, and stir fried the onion (cut into quarter-rounds) along with eggplant and garlic (pressed, one clove);

It is impossible to layer eggplant on one level, zucchini in another, and individual layers for mushrooms, peppers (capsicum), tomatoes. so I mixed the last three items together and made one layer. In addition, I added a bottom layer of marinara sauce and topped it off with another layer of marinara sauce. 
Secondly, 1 1/2 liters is half the size of container it should be. Thirdly, I had too many vegetables. 350 degrees minimum.

I did follow pretty much as written. I did start in the morning, tho, cutting and slicing. I put eggplant, onions and salt in one colander; the rest of veggies in another. left both on counter all day. Rendered out 1 1/2 c liquid. Still pretty easy to layer into aluminum pan with Italian mix shredded cheese. Family enjoyed. Hubby raised on Italian mountain farm and he liked it a lot.
Followed method exactly . 350°f 45 minutes... Everything still raw. Not sure which parts of the recipe was missing ... Bake on top rack? Cover with foil? Double the cooking time?
Great recipe, so easy to follow. I baked the ratatouille in a cast iron dutch oven and substituted the vinegar/water for the alcohol and added fresh basil. Thanks for sharing 😊
I don’t bother with layering the veggies. I cook everything in my cast iron pot and add sausage to it for my teenage son.
I added Italian shredded cheese as well as parm. Slices veggies instead of cubed. Garlic salt on one layer.
I love this combo of flavors! Authentic or not, I add mushrooms, black olives and capers to mine, and a splash of balsamic vinegar. It's incredible!
I would have like more details on how thick to cut the vegetables, and I think a whole onion was way too much. I tasted onion all night and the next morning.
sauteed julienne red peppers and onions and used as one of the the layers. grated a hunk of pecorino romano just because that's what I had. added a nice bite
